To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a Bayesian approach to the discovery of linear acyclic causal graphs can be developed that is both theoretically and empirically superior to the state of the art; (2) the approach is applicable to a wider range of distributions than the state of the-art; and (3) the approach is implemented in an open source code package.

We develop a new Bayesian score for linear acyclic causal model estimation, which can be applied to non-Gaussian data, and is able to express the relative certainty of the estimated causal relationships.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What is the best method for estimating linear causal models from data?
the problem of learning causal relationships between a set of variables from observational data.
the development of methods for automated discovery of linear acyclic causal relationships from non-experimental data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is the best method for learning linear acyclic causal networks from non-intervention data.
we provide a method that, for a very modest size networks is as good as, or better, than all other methods.

the method presented in this paper is the first Bayesian score-based approach for linear acyclic causal model estimation that is able to utilize non Gaussianity in the data and is also able to express the degree to which the estimated model is certain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed Bayesian approach can be used for causal inference from both Gaussian and non-Gaussian data, and it has a better accuracy than the state-of-the-art method for non-Gaussian data.

we have developed a new Bayesian score-based method to discover linear acyclic causal model from non-intervention data, and we have shown that this new method is more accurate than the previous methods on small scale networks.
we provide the first method for estimating the posterior probability distribution over the set of linear acyclic causal graphs consistent with a given set of data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Bayesian score is able to take advantage both of the non-Gaussianity and the non-linearity of the data, and that the Bayesian score-based approach is a viable and competitive alternative to existing approaches.
, while the problem of learning causal relationships from data is difficult, there are still many ways to approach it.
, in order to fully exploit the power of Bayesian methods in causal inference, it is essential to develop Bayesian methods that are able to take advantage also of non-Gaussian features of the data.
